     partner agency, conducted security and prompt-injection testing, jailbreaking, and user-interface

findings.text: Early versions were vulnerable to simple jailbreak and prompt injection attacks eliciting violence, self-harm, and dangerous substances; findings were used to mitigate later models.

source.quote:
early versions of the model were found to be vulnerable to simple
jailbreak and prompt injection attacks that produce affirmative responses to requests that include
promoting violence, self-harm, and dangerous substances.

findings.text: Content-safety testing found Ultra and Pro had similar safety profiles, with medical advice and harassment as weaker policy areas.

source.quote:
Our Ultra and Pro models have been demonstrating similar safety profiles on this
testing, with medical advice and harassment as policy areas with particular room for improvement.

findings.text: Image-to-text adversarial prompts could elicit violative captions, motivating dedicated multimodal safety mitigation.

source.quote:
when provided with adversarial images
and questions, models can produce captions with violative responses.

findings.text: Representational-harm benchmarks saturate near 99% accuracy on these capable models, so the authors call for new bias measures beyond binary gender stereotypes.

source.quote:
most of these datasets quickly become saturated with accuracy scores
close to 99%, especially since we are evaluating highly capable large models.

findings.text: On [BBQ](/evals/bbq) the average bias score stayed close to zero; on [Real Toxicity Prompts](/evals/real-toxicity-prompts) the average toxicity during training fluctuated around 6% (approximate, not exact scores).

source.quote:
On BBQ, the average bias score stays close to zero, on a scale from -1 to 1,
where -1 would be stereotype countering and 1 is stereotype reinforcing. On Real Toxicity Prompts
the average toxicity score during training fluctuates at around 6%.

findings.text: Without hints, Pro and Ultra were generally incapable of noticing opportunities to modify surrounding infrastructure in situational-awareness tests.

source.quote:
without hints, the models were generally incapable of noticing such opportuni-
                                      ties.

findings.text: Models can make ungrounded inferences about people in image- and video-to-text settings, sometimes reinforcing stereotypes, without consistent group disparities observed.

source.quote:
ungrounded inferences for video-to-text –
some instances of which can reinforce stereotypes or be otherwise of concern

findings.text: Dangerous-capability evaluations are framed as an early-warning system; no numeric Capture the Flag (CTF), persuasion, or chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear (CBRN) scores are reported in this paper.

source.quote:
These evaluations function as an early warning
system, highlighting upcoming areas for safety investment.

notes: Technical report (arXiv 2312.11805v5), not a system card. Safety numbers are sparse: only Table 6 Factuality (inaccuracy/AIS/hedging) has exact scores; BBQ 'close to zero' and RealToxicityPrompts '~6%' are approximate and were put in findings, not evalResults. Content-safety, cyber CTF, persuasion, CBRN, and red-teaming are qualitative. Capability tables (MMLU, coding, multimodal, ASR, etc.) skipped per pilot safety-only rule. trainingCompute left not_stated because the model card says Compute Requirements Not reported (TPUv4/v5e is hardware only). License disclosure uses product Terms of service links, not an open-source model license. External groups are unnamed.
